name: encoding-utf16
algorithm: UTF-16LE to UTF-8 of a mixed-script line (ASCII, Latin-1, Cyrillic, CJK, one astral scalar) repeated n times, rounds times, each language's standard decoder; the checksum adds per round the output length and one output byte at a moving index (README.md).

skip.c: no UTF-16 decoder in C's standard library (mbrtoc16 is the other direction and locale-bound)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the decoder is tested by the lane's Go tests (TestStdEncoding_WptCases, TestStdEncoding_DecodeAdversarial)
notes: Mk: encoding.Utf16Le.Decode into an arena reset each round (sized in one pass, written in a second: Mk's API). Rust: char::decode_utf16 over units read from the bytes, into one String reused. Zig: std.unicode.utf16LeToUtf8 over an aligned []u16 made once, into one buffer. Go: utf16.DecodeRune and utf8.AppendRune into one buffer reused.
Checksums agree among Go, Mk, Rust and Zig at both sizes on the owner's machine (std-encoding session 1, 2026-11-12).
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
